extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/agents and other practitioners before the USPTO; respondents in USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal-discipline proceedings; OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing reciprocal disciplinary proceedings under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 and related USPTO disciplinary actions (exclusion from practice, publication, notification, and administrative restrictions). Applicable when a practitioner has been disciplined by a state authority and the USPTO is asked to impose reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline upon a practitioner identical to the discipline imposed by a state court or other duly constituted authority when that authority has disciplined the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings are brought pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 and 35 U.S.C. § 32; the USPTO can order exclusion from practice in trademark and other non-patent matters based on state disbarment. The Complaint requests reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by the state authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and Order timeline and service (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' must be sent to the respondent notifying them that a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline has been filed and giving them an opportunity to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order is sent by certified mail and provides the respondent 40 days to file a response opposing reciprocal discipline. The Notice in this matter was delivered on May 17, 2017 (certified mail receipt cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible grounds to oppose reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order specifically permits opposition only on the statutory grounds enumerated in § 11.24(d)(1); respondents must assert those grounds within the 40-day period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, the USPTO may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose the reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's failure to file a response in this case resulted in the determination that there was no genuine issue of material fact and that exclusion was appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion from practice before the USPTO in trademark and non-patent matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is excluded from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO, effective the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order effectuates exclusion; the order and its effective date are set forth in the Final Order pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette describing the exclusion and the reasons for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs OED Director to publish the provided 'NOTICE OF EXCLUSION' text in the Official Gazette, including the respondent's name, nature of suspension, predicate state disciplinary action, and summary of misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required notice content – particulars of misconduct and rules violated
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Exclusion should summarize the misconduct that led to the state discipline (e.g., failing to competently represent clients, failing to file a brief, failing to obtain visas, failing to communicate, failing to perform paid work, mishandling client funds, delaying proceedings, failing to respond to Bar Counsel, and conduct harming perception of the profession) and list the specific professional conduct rules violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the Notice lists violations of Maryland Lawyers' Rules of Professional Conduct 1.1, 1.3, 1.4(a)(2), 1.5(a), 1.15(c), 3.2, 3.4(c), 8.1(b), 8.4(a) and 8.4(d) as the predicates for exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give notice to disciplinary enforcement agencies and public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final Order directs the OED Director to provide those notices to relevant state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public as required by § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's duties under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is required to comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 as part of the disciplinary order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifically directs the respondent to comply with the duties in § 11.58; the order does not restate those duties but makes compliance mandatory as part of the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of Respondent's name from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This administrative action severs the respondent's association with USPTO electronic access and credentials tied to Customer Numbers and PKI certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall the respondent have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order bars the respondent from acquiring or being added to Customer Numbers or reestablishing related electronic access until reinstatement is granted by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority and public availability of disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, and disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites statutory/regulatory authority and provides the FOIA Reading Room URL for reviewing disciplinary decisions.
